root: ^Oh, Henry, dear, you know how much I dislike you calling me that.
^And YOU know how much I dislike you calling me Henry.
^Well, fine. (Both chuckle.) It’s been too long, darling. And to answer your question, I’m absolutely dreadful.

Paridise: ^...I found the other woman. Some poor, sweet twenty-something. When I heard, I nearly chucked my pocketbook out the window.
Surprise: ^You’re right, of course. But it hurts, all the same... I had a life before the Don, you know.
^Do I ever! I remember when every club promoter in the city would saw a leg off to hear you sing.
^And now... look at me! I’m washed up! He’s gotta pay. Hank? Will you do me a favor? (A beat. The grisly implication of her request hangs in the air.)
^I don’t like where this is going.
Going: ^I don’t like where this is going.
^It doesn’t matter. With the Tagliatelle land grab, he’ll be swimming with the fishes by St Patrick’s either way. I’ll just be expediting the process. Besides, you won’t be implicated.
Baloney: ^He’s more in love with his position.

c-0: ^He’s more in love with his position.
^Well, my husband will leave a vacuum.
^And you think that slimeball can fill his shoes?
^You’re gonna be the death of me

Death: ^(sighs.) You’re gonna be the death of me.
^The cab slows, turning onto a busy downtown street filled with neon lights and bustling silhouettes.
^Nonsense. You’re going to be the death of my husband. (She hands him a thick envelope.)
^The cab pulls up to SAMBUCA, the Pappardelle crime family’s downtown base.
^I pray you’re right. Now, split before I change my mind. And–(he kisses her hand) knock ‘em dead.

c-0: ^You won’t regret this. (She exits the vehicle, slinks away, and disappears into SAMBUCA.)
